content.user_title: Design Event Stores for Event-Sourced Systems
content.value_statement: Event-sourced systems need durable, ordered event storage with safe replay and concurrency controls. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through schemas, technology choices, and implementation patterns.
actual_capabilities: Compares EventStoreDB, PostgreSQL, Kafka, DynamoDB, and Marten for event store use cases.
Provides a PostgreSQL schema for events, snapshots, and subscription checkpoints.
Shows Python examples for appending, reading, and subscribing to events.
Explains optimistic concurrency, stream ordering, global ordering, and idempotency.
Offers operational guidance for replay safety, projections, snapshots, and indexes.
limitations: Examples are templates and must be adapted before production use.
It does not run live benchmarks or inspect a deployed event store.
It does not replace architecture review for compliance, scale, or recovery needs.
Security controls, access policies, and encryption choices remain environment-specific.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Event Store
use_cases.description: Define storage requirements, stream layout, versioning, and technology options before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Implement Event Persistence
use_cases.description: Use schema and code templates to create append-only event storage with optimistic concurrency.

use_cases.title: Review Replay and Projection Safety
use_cases.description: Check subscription checkpoints, idempotent handlers, rebuild flows, and snapshot policy before release.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Store
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose an event store for a new event-sourced service. Compare PostgreSQL, EventStoreDB, Kafka, and DynamoDB for my workload.

prompt_templates.title: Design the Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a PostgreSQL event store schema for my aggregate streams. Include event rows, snapshots, checkpoints, indexes, and concurrency rules.

prompt_templates.title: Draft the Implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an implementation plan for append, read-stream, read-all, and subscription operations using async Python and PostgreSQL.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this event store design for replay safety, projection rebuilds, idempotency, snapshot policy, retention, and operational risks.

output_examples.input: I need an event store for an order service using PostgreSQL.
output: A recommended table structure for events, snapshots, and subscription checkpoints.
Index choices for stream reads, global subscriptions, event type queries, and time-based queries.
Concurrency and replay guidance for append-only writes and projection rebuilds.

output_examples.input: Compare EventStoreDB and DynamoDB for a serverless event-sourced system.
output: A comparison of operational fit, query patterns, concurrency support, and scaling tradeoffs.
A short recommendation based on team skills, cloud constraints, throughput, and replay needs.

output_examples.input: Review my subscription design before production launch.
output: A checklist covering checkpoints, idempotent handlers, retry behavior, backpressure, and rebuild strategy.
Specific risks to test before enabling production projections.

best_practices: Start by stating aggregate types, expected throughput, replay needs, and retention requirements.
Ask for technology tradeoffs before selecting a storage engine or schema shape.
Validate generated designs with load tests, failure tests, and production recovery drills.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the templates as drop-in production code without testing and adaptation.
Do not ignore idempotency, backpressure, or replay safety in projection handlers.
Do not store large mutable documents when small immutable events are sufficient.

faq.question: What does this skill help design?
faq.answer: It helps design event stores for event-sourced systems, including schemas, streams, subscriptions, and replay workflows.

faq.question: Can it choose an event store technology?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares options such as EventStoreDB, PostgreSQL, Kafka, DynamoDB, and Marten based on requirements.

faq.question: Does it provide implementation examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Python-oriented examples for appending, reading, subscribing, and using EventStoreDB or DynamoDB.

faq.question: Is the generated code production-ready?
faq.answer: No. The examples are starting points and need testing, security review, and environment-specific changes.

faq.question: Does it cover projection rebuild safety?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends checkpoints, idempotent handlers, clean rebuild flows, and replay-safe processing.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
